title: Raft under a leader failure
note: A replay of a recorded real session in three of its real turns: @builder’s turn that handed the app to @critic, @critic’s first review, and @builder’s first turn that started after that review. Each says that turn’s words, shows the last version it made, and reports its recorded cost. recordedTurns lists every real turn; notReplayed names the ones the replay leaves out, and edits what it changes.
ask: @builder How does Raft keep a cluster consistent when the leader dies in the middle of a write? I want to see it, not read about it: a five-node cluster I can poke. Let me kill the leader or any node, partition the network, send writes and change the election timeouts, and watch terms, votes and the log replicate, conflict and get repaired.

said: The simulator is working. I’m checking the browser test result, then I’ll post it for review.
Fixing one last small-text warning at 375 px, then checking the dark theme.

I built a live five-node Raft cluster you can break. Press **Play: leader dies mid-write** and watch it. The leader adds two writes, sends only the first to one neighbor, then crashes. A new leader wins with a higher term (node colors change with the term). When the old leader restarts, it gets a red-struck conflict in the log grid and its write that only it held turns red under Client writes as lost.

You can also do it by hand:
- **Crash and restart:** click any node.
- **Partitions:** cut links one at a time, or use **Isolate leader** or **Split 2 | 3**. A leader on the losing side keeps taking writes that never commit.
- **Election timeouts:** drag the slider below 100 ms and elections start piling up.
- **Log repair:** the orange ▲ markers step back one index at a time as the leader finds where a follower’s log matches its own.

Postbox’s browser check passes at 375 and 1280 px. I could only look at it in the light theme; it uses only theme colors, so dark should be fine, but I haven’t seen it.

@critic, please review the app.
I’ll inspect the live app and its source, then pin concrete issues to the review.

Requested changes with four pinned comments. The main issues are the claim that minority-held writes always disappear, the hidden client destination after partitions, log cells losing their labels as writes accumulate, and truncated event explanations on phones.

There’s nothing left to fix. Those warnings came from the checks on v1 and v3. Postbox’s check on v4, the version showing now, passed. The current file has the changes that cleared each warning:

- **Small text:** every label in the chart, including the “term N” inside each node, is now big enough to show at 12 px or more on a 375 px screen.
- **Faint dashes:** the dashed outlines are coarser (6 px dashes with 4 px gaps), and the empty slots in the log grid are now thin solid outlines.
- **Cut-off text:** the explanation at the bottom of the log chart was being clipped, so it now sits in a separate key below the chart.

I haven’t opened a new review because the version under review hasn’t changed. That review stays open for critic.
v5 renders correctly. I’m checking the browser test, then I’ll resolve critic’s threads.

I’ve shipped v5 of the simulator with all four of critic’s comments addressed. All four threads on the review are marked resolved, each with a one-line answer.

- **Takeaway:** it now says a write commits only once 3 of 5 nodes hold it in the leader’s own term. A write the leader dies holding survives if the next leader has it and is overwritten if not. The mid-write scenario now says which of its two writes survives.
- **Write target:** chips beside **Send write** pick which leader gets your writes. If the client is still writing to a stale leader, a warning shows in the middle of the ring.
- **Log and history:** the log grid scrolls sideways instead of squeezing cells, and clicking a cell shows its entry. The event history now wraps and expands to the last 300 events.

Postbox’s browser check passes on v5.

app.title: Raft, live: five nodes, one log
app.intent: Only majority-held entries survive a leader crash; minority entries get overwritten by the next leader.
app.code:
Raft, live: five nodes, one log

A write is safe only once a majority holds it. When a leader dies mid-write, the next leader’s log wins and anything held by a minority is overwritten.

Click a node to crash or restart it. Click a link to cut or heal it. Heartbeats every 50 ms; network delay 30–55 ms. Try an election timeout under 100 ms.

Cluster
RequestVote AppendEntries reply election timer left color = term
Replicated logs (cell = entry, number = its term)
log index → committed on that node not yet leader’s nextIndex leader
Client writesdashed = pending · committed · lost

review.title: Raft, live: five nodes, one log
review.fallback: Review of Raft, live: five nodes, one log: comment in the chat.

comments.text: The opening takeaway says anything held by a minority is overwritten, but an uncommitted entry can survive when a node holding it wins the election. The scenario itself sends the first orphan to a potential winner. Change the takeaway to say uncommitted writes may survive or be overwritten; distinguish the first orphan’s possible survival from the second orphan’s loss. Also qualify majority-based commitment with Raft’s current-term rule.

After a partition, curLeader() labels the highest-term leader in the center, while write() keeps routing to S.clientLeader, potentially the isolated old leader. The visible leader and the write destination can therefore disagree without a persistent cue. Show the client’s connected node beside Send write and let the reader select which leader receives it, so minority-side pending writes have an explicit cause.

renderLog() squeezes every accumulated entry into the same 400-unit SVG. Beyond roughly 17 entries W drops below 20 and all entry-term labels disappear; further writes eventually produce unusable cell widths. Keep a minimum cell width with horizontal scrolling or a movable index window, and retain readable terms and commands for the selected entry.

The event rows force nowrap with hidden overflow and ellipsis, which cuts off the explanation of votes, rejection, and conflicts at phone width. There is no way to expand or inspect the truncated text, and only six events survive. Wrap the rows and provide a paused or expandable event history so the reader can recover why the log changed.
